$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,2\le x\le 3,\,\,1\le y\le 4\}.$ Find the radius of gyration of the plate about the $x$-axis." :question/worked-solution "For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{x}$ about the $x$-axis is given by
${R}_{x}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{x}$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{y}$ about the $y$-axis is given by
${R}_{y}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{y}$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by
${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is defined as

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function.

The area of the rectangular plate $D$ is $A=1\cdot 3=3.$ Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by

$$
\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{A}=\frac{M}{3}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{M}{3}{\int }_{1}^{4}{\int }_{2}^{3}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{3}{\int }_{1}^{4}[x{y}^{2}]_{x=2}^{x=3}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{3}{\int }_{1}^{4}3{y}^{2}-2{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{3}{\int }_{1}^{4}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{3}{[\frac{1}{3}{y}^{3}]}_{1}^{4} \\  & =\frac{M}{3}(\frac{64}{3}-\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =\frac{M}{3}\cdot 21 \\  & =7M.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
{R}_{x}^{2}=7\,⇒\,{R}_{x}=\sqrt{7}.
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-80bbb187-dc3c-5b0f-ba62-a0ca8ff3dda3"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-80bbb187-dc3c-5b0f-ba62-a0ca8ff3dda3" :answer-field/id #uuid "80bbb187-dc3c-5b0f-ba62-a0ca8ff3dda3" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-974dc7bd-feb4-507f-bf72-f126baafb27c" :answer-field/choices ["answer-77cb1250-c861-5412-bfeb-953b40015636" "answer-886e0c3d-268d-59a3-b4e6-c11fe4f62ef9" "answer-974dc7bd-feb4-507f-bf72-f126baafb27c" "answer-1c55e985-99d7-510d-94c4-cdefd528164b" "answer-3db4c8ac-db31-5972-9d3f-65cb573f87d8"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-77cb1250-c861-5412-bfeb-953b40015636" :answer/id #uuid "77cb1250-c861-5412-bfeb-953b40015636" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{21}}{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-886e0c3d-268d-59a3-b4e6-c11fe4f62ef9" :answer/id #uuid "886e0c3d-268d-59a3-b4e6-c11fe4f62ef9" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\sqrt{14}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-974dc7bd-feb4-507f-bf72-f126baafb27c" :answer/id #uuid "974dc7bd-feb4-507f-bf72-f126baafb27c" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\sqrt{7}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1c55e985-99d7-510d-94c4-cdefd528164b" :answer/id #uuid "1c55e985-99d7-510d-94c4-cdefd528164b" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\sqrt{\frac{17}{2}}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3db4c8ac-db31-5972-9d3f-65cb573f87d8" :answer/id #uuid "3db4c8ac-db31-5972-9d3f-65cb573f87d8" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\sqrt{\frac{34}{3}}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-a8f6939e-ee8d-5d31-921b-202a2621754c" :question/id #uuid "a8f6939e-ee8d-5d31-921b-202a2621754c" :question/math-academy-id "q-163581" :question/problem "A rectangular plate of mass $M$ and uniform mass density occupies the region
$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 5,\,\,0\le y\le 3\}.$ Find the radius of gyration of the plate about the $x$-axis." :question/worked-solution "For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{x}$ about the $x$-axis is given by
${R}_{x}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{x}$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{y}$ about the $y$-axis is given by
${R}_{y}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{y}$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by
${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is defined as

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function.

The area of the rectangular plate $D$ is $A=4\cdot 3=12.$ Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by

$$
\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{A}=\frac{M}{12}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{M}{12}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{1}^{5}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{12}{\int }_{0}^{3}[x{y}^{2}]_{x=1}^{x=5}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{12}{\int }_{0}^{3}5{y}^{2}-{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{12}{\int }_{0}^{3}4{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{12}{[\frac{4}{3}{y}^{3}]}_{0}^{3} \\  & =\frac{M}{12}(36-0) \\  & =3M.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
{R}_{x}^{2}=3\,⇒\,{R}_{x}=\sqrt{3}.
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-2bb25b16-fefe-543c-8d2a-1f870068fdf2"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-2bb25b16-fefe-543c-8d2a-1f870068fdf2" :answer-field/id #uuid "2bb25b16-fefe-543c-8d2a-1f870068fdf2" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-014bd219-6bb7-5591-94da-c8e05e6257db" :answer-field/choices ["answer-52222829-b82c-52b5-a96b-b5832b8620cb" "answer-033f9c9a-b36b-5812-9012-d79d61e31523" "answer-014bd219-6bb7-5591-94da-c8e05e6257db" "answer-40971c50-7326-5588-bfcf-cffa95a31ea9" "answer-e0f7f856-a434-5213-900c-1eab2db4aba9"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-52222829-b82c-52b5-a96b-b5832b8620cb" :answer/id #uuid "52222829-b82c-52b5-a96b-b5832b8620cb" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-033f9c9a-b36b-5812-9012-d79d61e31523" :answer/id #uuid "033f9c9a-b36b-5812-9012-d79d61e31523" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-014bd219-6bb7-5591-94da-c8e05e6257db" :answer/id #uuid "014bd219-6bb7-5591-94da-c8e05e6257db" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\sqrt{3}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-40971c50-7326-5588-bfcf-cffa95a31ea9" :answer/id #uuid "40971c50-7326-5588-bfcf-cffa95a31ea9" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\sqrt{\frac{5}{3}}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-e0f7f856-a434-5213-900c-1eab2db4aba9" :answer/id #uuid "e0f7f856-a434-5213-900c-1eab2db4aba9" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\sqrt{\frac{7}{2}}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-cba3666c-1980-5c09-82de-e7dd19c40b69" :question/id #uuid "cba3666c-1980-5c09-82de-e7dd19c40b69" :question/math-academy-id "q-163575" :question/problem "A rectangular plate of mass $M$ and uniform mass density occupies the region

$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,3\le x\le 5,\,\,2\le y\le 4\}.$ Find the radius of gyration of the plate about the $y$-axis." :question/worked-solution "For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{x}$ about the $x$-axis is given by

where ${I}_{x}$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

where ${I}_{y}$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by
${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is defined as

$$
{I}_{y}={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function.

The area of the rectangular plate $D$ is $A=2\cdot 2=4.$ Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by

$$
\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{A}=\frac{M}{4}.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{M}{4}{\int }_{2}^{4}{\int }_{3}^{5}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{4}{\int }_{2}^{4}{[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{3}^{5}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{4}{\int }_{2}^{4}(\frac{125}{3}-9)\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{4}{\int }_{2}^{4}\frac{98}{3}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{4}{[\frac{98}{3}y]}_{2}^{4} \\  & =\frac{49M}{6}\cdot (4-2) \\  & =\frac{49M}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
{R}_{y}^{2}=\frac{49}{3}\,⇒\,{R}_{y}=\sqrt{\frac{49}{3}}=\frac{7}{\sqrt{3}}.
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-6481d0c5-9b18-592d-a5aa-357b3fbca57b"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-6481d0c5-9b18-592d-a5aa-357b3fbca57b" :answer-field/id #uuid "6481d0c5-9b18-592d-a5aa-357b3fbca57b" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-91a40d38-352d-5174-8eee-24d0d573f67c" :answer-field/choices ["answer-c6f45d1c-6eee-552d-b559-5553e3c33b7d" "answer-901a1aa5-f9b9-54e8-b4e1-ed9066218fc9" "answer-91a40d38-352d-5174-8eee-24d0d573f67c" "answer-d7589253-2194-5059-b7cf-fc834480c4ed" "answer-a72adde0-d637-5df5-9d74-b56a66f4cfac"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-c6f45d1c-6eee-552d-b559-5553e3c33b7d" :answer/id #uuid "c6f45d1c-6eee-552d-b559-5553e3c33b7d" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "2\sqrt{5}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-901a1aa5-f9b9-54e8-b4e1-ed9066218fc9" :answer/id #uuid "901a1aa5-f9b9-54e8-b4e1-ed9066218fc9" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{3\sqrt{7}}{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-91a40d38-352d-5174-8eee-24d0d573f67c" :answer/id #uuid "91a40d38-352d-5174-8eee-24d0d573f67c" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{7}{\sqrt{3}}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-d7589253-2194-5059-b7cf-fc834480c4ed" :answer/id #uuid "d7589253-2194-5059-b7cf-fc834480c4ed" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\sqrt{14}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-a72adde0-d637-5df5-9d74-b56a66f4cfac" :answer/id #uuid "a72adde0-d637-5df5-9d74-b56a66f4cfac" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\sqrt{\frac{41}{2}}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-464dc60e-dfa3-5c24-8df3-bdca1e567180" :question/id #uuid "464dc60e-dfa3-5c24-8df3-bdca1e567180" :question/math-academy-id "q-163608" :question/problem "A rectangular plate of mass $M$ and uniform mass density occupies the region

"A plate of mass $M$ occupies the region $D$ bounded by the lines $y=2x,$ $x=1,$ and the $x$-axis. Its mass density at any point on the plate is given by $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{3M}{2}x.$ Find the radius of gyration of the plate about the origin." :question/worked-solution "For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{x}$ about the $x$-axis is given by
${R}_{x}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{x}$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{y}$ about the $y$-axis is given by
${R}_{y}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{y}$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by
${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

The moment of inertia about the origin is defined as

$$
{I}_{0}={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function. The region $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le 2x\}.
$$

Hence, the moment of inertia about the origin is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{0} & ={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\cdot \frac{3M}{2}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2x}{x}^{3}+x{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{[{x}^{3}y+\frac{1}{3}x{y}^{3}]}_{y=0}^{y=2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}2{x}^{4}+\frac{8}{3}{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{14}{3}{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{[\frac{14}{15}{x}^{5}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}\cdot \frac{14}{15} \\  & =\frac{7M}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of gyration about the origin is

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{0} & =\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{7M}{5}\cdot \frac{1}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{7}{5}}.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-96a67bd8-ef2e-5ca9-867f-c8028ad58f33"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-96a67bd8-ef2e-5ca9-867f-c8028ad58f33" :answer-field/id #uuid "96a67bd8-ef2e-5ca9-867f-c8028ad58f33" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-dac54592-73f2-5539-95af-9b181dfbbc6d" :answer-field/choices ["answer-17408f30-0e49-5024-8582-e77ea33d1531" "answer-c3244fd4-d2f9-5e9c-ab2f-2bf3f05ed94e" "answer-5c870d2c-e72b-5ed4-9ac6-a6bac8e306d7" "answer-1aa03666-f99f-5788-82b2-6a8cfc4ed4a0" "answer-dac54592-73f2-5539-95af-9b181dfbbc6d"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-17408f30-0e49-5024-8582-e77ea33d1531" :answer/id #uuid "17408f30-0e49-5024-8582-e77ea33d1531" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "1" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-c3244fd4-d2f9-5e9c-ab2f-2bf3f05ed94e" :answer/id #uuid "c3244fd4-d2f9-5e9c-ab2f-2bf3f05ed94e" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{8}{9}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-5c870d2c-e72b-5ed4-9ac6-a6bac8e306d7" :answer/id #uuid "5c870d2c-e72b-5ed4-9ac6-a6bac8e306d7" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{15}}{4}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1aa03666-f99f-5788-82b2-6a8cfc4ed4a0" :answer/id #uuid "1aa03666-f99f-5788-82b2-6a8cfc4ed4a0" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-dac54592-73f2-5539-95af-9b181dfbbc6d" :answer/id #uuid "dac54592-73f2-5539-95af-9b181dfbbc6d" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\sqrt{\frac{7}{5}}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-e0566907-74aa-5b66-a065-487764f08eb0" :question/id #uuid "e0566907-74aa-5b66-a065-487764f08eb0" :question/math-academy-id "q-38823" :question/problem "A plate of mass $M$ occupies the region $D$ bounded by the lines $y=x,$ $x=1,$ and the $x$-axis. Its mass density at any point on the plate is given by $\lambda (x,y)=8Mxy.$ Find the radius of gyration of the plate about the origin." :question/worked-solution "For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{x}$ about the $x$-axis is given by

where ${I}_{x}$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{y}$ about the $y$-axis is given by
${R}_{y}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{y}$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by
${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

The moment of inertia about the origin is defined as

$$
{I}_{0}={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function. The region $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$

Hence, the moment of inertia about the origin is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{0} & ={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\cdot 8Mxy\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =8M{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}{x}^{3}y+x{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =8M{\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{3}{y}^{2}+\frac{1}{4}x{y}^{4}]}_{y=0}^{y=x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =8M{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{2}{x}^{5}+\frac{1}{4}{x}^{5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =8M{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3}{4}{x}^{5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =M{\int }_{0}^{1}6{x}^{5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =M[{x}^{6}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =M.\end{aligned}

$$

Hence, the moment of inertia about the origin is

$$

$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186281686 :question/worked-solution "For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

Therefore, the radius of gyration about the $x$-axis is

Its mass density at any point is given by $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡2}.$ Find the radius of gyration of the plate about the $y$-axis." :question/worked-solution "For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{x}$ about the $x$-axis is given by
${R}_{x}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{x}$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{y}$ about the $y$-axis is given by
${R}_{y}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{y}$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by
${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

In polar coordinates, the region occupied by the plate is given by

$$
D=\{(r,\theta )\,:\,1\le r\le \sqrt{2},\,\,-\frac{\pi }{4}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{4}\}.
$$

The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis, in polar coordinates, is defined as

$$
{I}_{y}={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta ,
$$

where $\lambda (r,\theta )$ is the mass density function.

Also, the mass density in terms of polar coordinates is $\lambda (r,\theta )=\frac{M}{{r}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{ln}⁡2}.$
Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{M}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4}{\int }_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}r\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{M}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}({\int }_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}r\,\text{d}r)({\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4}\,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{M}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}{r}^{2}{|}_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \theta {|}_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4} \\  & =\frac{M}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\cdot (1-\frac{1}{2})\cdot \frac{\pi }{2} \\  & =\frac{\pi M}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of gyration about the $x$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{y} & =\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{\pi M}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\cdot \frac{1}{M}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\frac{\pi }{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}}.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-d338a349-3b9f-5d71-b3f4-8e6e22455c77"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 0.$ Its mass density at any point is given by $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{\pi }({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}).$ Find the radius of gyration of the plate about the origin." :question/worked-solution "For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{x}$ about the $x$-axis is given by
${R}_{x}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{x}$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{y}$ about the $y$-axis is given by
${R}_{y}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{y}$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by
${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

In polar coordinates, the region occupied by the plate is given by

$$
D=\{(r,\theta )\,:\,0\le r\le \sqrt{2},\,\,0\le \theta \le \pi \}.
$$

The moment of inertia about the origin, in polar coordinates, is defined as

$$
{I}_{0}={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta ,
$$

where $\lambda (r,\theta )$ is the mass density function.

Also, the mass density in terms of polar coordinates is $\lambda (r,\theta )=\frac{M}{\pi }{r}^{2}.$
Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{0} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{M}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}{r}^{5}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{M}{\pi }({\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}{r}^{5}\,\text{d}r)({\int }_{0}^{\pi }\,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{M}{\pi }\cdot \frac{1}{6}{r}^{6}{|}_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \theta {|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =\frac{M}{\pi }\cdot \frac{8}{6}\cdot \pi  \\  & =\frac{4M}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of gyration about the $x$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{0} & =\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{4M}{3}\cdot \frac{1}{M}} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-bef2f558-3cf7-59d6-9515-914459e1240b"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-bef2f558-3cf7-59d6-9515-914459e1240b" :answer-field/id #uuid "bef2f558-3cf7-59d6-9515-914459e1240b" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-fc266323-7418-5bae-b2ea-93950027798c" :answer-field/choices ["answer-e774e4c8-1628-5af4-a5cd-f971dd1a0058" "answer-80a333aa-bc0f-5028-8ed7-d5417e844298" "answer-fc266323-7418-5bae-b2ea-93950027798c" "answer-cced5037-72cd-5ef9-9fd4-3ab7e34f2a09" "answer-ae9c1715-3633-57e9-8d5b-964a10452511"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-e774e4c8-1628-5af4-a5cd-f971dd1a0058" :answer/id #uuid "e774e4c8-1628-5af4-a5cd-f971dd1a0058" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-80a333aa-bc0f-5028-8ed7-d5417e844298" :answer/id #uuid "80a333aa-bc0f-5028-8ed7-d5417e844298" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-fc266323-7418-5bae-b2ea-93950027798c" :answer/id #uuid "fc266323-7418-5bae-b2ea-93950027798c" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-cced5037-72cd-5ef9-9fd4-3ab7e34f2a09" :answer/id #uuid "cced5037-72cd-5ef9-9fd4-3ab7e34f2a09" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{3}{4}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-ae9c1715-3633-57e9-8d5b-964a10452511" :answer/id #uuid "ae9c1715-3633-57e9-8d5b-964a10452511" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\sqrt{\frac{3}{5}}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186284392 :question/worked-solution "For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{x}$ about the $x$-axis is given by
${R}_{x}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{x}$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{y}$ about the $y$-axis is given by
${R}_{y}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{y}$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by
${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

In polar coordinates, the region occupied by the plate is given by

$$
D=\{(r,\theta )\,:\,1\le r\le 2,\,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi \}.
$$

The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis, in polar coordinates, is defined as

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta ,
$$

where $\lambda (r,\theta )$ is the mass density function.

Also, the mass density in terms of polar coordinates is $\lambda (r,\theta )=\frac{3}{14\pi }Mr.$
Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{3}{14\pi }M{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{1}^{2}{r}^{4}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{3M}{14\pi }({\int }_{1}^{2}{r}^{4}\,\text{d}r)({\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{3M}{14\pi }\cdot \frac{1}{5}{r}^{5}{|}_{1}^{2}\cdot ({\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\frac{(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta )}{2}\,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{3M}{14\pi }\cdot \frac{31}{5}\cdot {[\frac{1}{2}\theta -\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta ]}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =\frac{3M}{14\pi }\cdot \frac{31}{5}\cdot \pi  \\  & =\frac{93M}{70}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of gyration about the $x$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{x} & =\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{93M}{70}\cdot \frac{1}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{93}{70}}.\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186369943 :question/worked-solution "For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{x}$ about the $x$-axis is given by
${R}_{x}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{x}$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{y}$ about the $y$-axis is given by
${R}_{y}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{y}$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by
${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

In polar coordinates, the region occupied by the plate is given by

$$
D=\{(r,\theta )\,:\,1\le r\le 2,\,\,\frac{\pi }{4}\le \theta \le \frac{3\pi }{4}\}.
$$

The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis, in polar coordinates, is defined as

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta ,
$$

where $\lambda (r,\theta )$ is the mass density function.

Also, the mass density in terms of polar coordinates is $\lambda (r,\theta )=\frac{M}{2r{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }.$
Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{M}{2}{\int }_{\pi /4}^{3\pi /4}{\int }_{1}^{2}{r}^{2}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{M}{2}({\int }_{1}^{2}{r}^{2}\,\text{d}r)({\int }_{\pi /4}^{3\pi /4}\,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{M}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{3}{r}^{3}{|}_{1}^{2}\cdot \theta {|}_{\pi /4}^{3\pi /4} \\  & =\frac{M}{2}\cdot \frac{7}{3}\cdot \frac{\pi }{2} \\  & =\frac{7\pi M}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of gyration about the $x$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{x} & =\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{7\pi M}{12}\cdot \frac{1}{M}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\frac{7\pi }{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186284397 :question/worked-solution "For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{x}$ about the $x$-axis is given by
${R}_{x}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{x}$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{y}$ about the $y$-axis is given by
${R}_{y}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{y}$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by
${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

In polar coordinates, the region occupied by the plate is given by

$$
D=\{(r,\theta )\,:\,0\le r\le \sqrt{3},\,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi \}.
$$

The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis, in polar coordinates, is defined as

$$
{I}_{y}={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta ,
$$

where $\lambda (r,\theta )$ is the mass density function.

Also, the mass density in terms of polar coordinates is $\lambda (r,\theta )=\frac{2}{9\pi }M{r}^{2}.$
Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{2}{9\pi }M{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}{r}^{5}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{2}{9\pi }M({\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}{r}^{5}\,\text{d}r)({\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{2}{9\pi }M\cdot \frac{1}{6}{r}^{6}{|}_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}({\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\frac{1+\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta }{2}\,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{2}{9\pi }M\cdot \frac{9}{2}\cdot {[\frac{\theta }{2}+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta }{4}]}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =\frac{M}{\pi }\cdot \pi  \\  & =M.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of gyration about the $x$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{y} & =\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{M\cdot \frac{1}{M}} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186199458 :tutorial/content "In this lesson, we discuss a concept analogous to *center of mass* that applies to rotating bodies.

Recall that the *center of mass* of a plane lamina is defined as the point $(\bar{x},\bar{y})$ in the coordinate plane where the entire mass of the lamina could be concentrated to produce the same *total moment* about the coordinate axes as the original laminar. 

Analogously, the **radius of gyration** of a plane lamina is the distance $R$ from an axis of rotation $L$ that the entire mass $M$ of the lamina would need to be concentrated to produce the same *moment of inertia* as the original lamina. 

![](images/c9/c9999bf30a93a857db731488739f0a640edc7b91de907cd772b777489a011fb8.png)

To derive an explicit formula for the radius of gyration, recall that the moment of inertia of a particle $P$ of mass $m$ at a distance of $r$ from an axis of rotation equals

$$
mr^2.
$$

So, for a particle of mass $M$ at a distance of $R$ from the axis of rotation $L,$ the moment of inertia about $L$ is given by

$$
MR^2.
$$

The radius of gyration is defined as the distance $R$ that a particle of mass $M$ must be placed to give the same moment of inertia as the original lamina. Therefore, it is the solution to the equation

$$
I = MR^2,
$$

where $I$ is the moment of inertia of the lamina about $L.$

Rearranging this equation, we find that the radius of gyration is given by

$$
R = \sqrt{\dfrac{I}{M}}.
$$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186198500 :activity/expected-seconds 1380.0 :db/ensure [:activity/validate]}]

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{x}$ about the $x$-axis is given by
${R}_{x}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{x}$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{y}$ about the $y$-axis is given by
${R}_{y}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{y}$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by
${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is defined as

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function.

The area of the rectangular plate $D$ is $A=1\cdot 3=3.$ Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by

$$
\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{A}=\frac{M}{3}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{M}{3}{\int }_{1}^{4}{\int }_{2}^{3}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{3}{\int }_{1}^{4}[x{y}^{2}]_{x=2}^{x=3}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{3}{\int }_{1}^{4}3{y}^{2}-2{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{3}{\int }_{1}^{4}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{3}{[\frac{1}{3}{y}^{3}]}_{1}^{4} \\  & =\frac{M}{3}(\frac{64}{3}-\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =\frac{M}{3}\cdot 21 \\  & =7M.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
{R}_{x}^{2}=7\,⇒\,{R}_{x}=\sqrt{7}.
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-80bbb187-dc3c-5b0f-ba62-a0ca8ff3dda3"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-80bbb187-dc3c-5b0f-ba62-a0ca8ff3dda3" :answer-field/id #uuid "80bbb187-dc3c-5b0f-ba62-a0ca8ff3dda3" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-974dc7bd-feb4-507f-bf72-f126baafb27c" :answer-field/choices ["answer-77cb1250-c861-5412-bfeb-953b40015636" "answer-886e0c3d-268d-59a3-b4e6-c11fe4f62ef9" "answer-974dc7bd-feb4-507f-bf72-f126baafb27c" "answer-1c55e985-99d7-510d-94c4-cdefd528164b" "answer-3db4c8ac-db31-5972-9d3f-65cb573f87d8"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-77cb1250-c861-5412-bfeb-953b40015636" :answer/id #uuid "77cb1250-c861-5412-bfeb-953b40015636" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{21}}{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-886e0c3d-268d-59a3-b4e6-c11fe4f62ef9" :answer/id #uuid "886e0c3d-268d-59a3-b4e6-c11fe4f62ef9" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\sqrt{14}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-974dc7bd-feb4-507f-bf72-f126baafb27c" :answer/id #uuid "974dc7bd-feb4-507f-bf72-f126baafb27c" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\sqrt{7}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1c55e985-99d7-510d-94c4-cdefd528164b" :answer/id #uuid "1c55e985-99d7-510d-94c4-cdefd528164b" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\sqrt{\frac{17}{2}}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-3db4c8ac-db31-5972-9d3f-65cb573f87d8" :answer/id #uuid "3db4c8ac-db31-5972-9d3f-65cb573f87d8" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\sqrt{\frac{34}{3}}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-a8f6939e-ee8d-5d31-921b-202a2621754c" :question/id #uuid "a8f6939e-ee8d-5d31-921b-202a2621754c" :question/math-academy-id "q-163581" :question/problem "A rectangular plate of mass $M$ and uniform mass density occupies the region
$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 5,\,\,0\le y\le 3\}.$ Find the radius of gyration of the plate about the $x$-axis." :question/worked-solution "For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{x}$ about the $x$-axis is given by
${R}_{x}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{x}$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{y}$ about the $y$-axis is given by
${R}_{y}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{y}$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by
${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is defined as

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function.

The area of the rectangular plate $D$ is $A=4\cdot 3=12.$ Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by

$$
\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{A}=\frac{M}{12}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{M}{12}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{1}^{5}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{12}{\int }_{0}^{3}[x{y}^{2}]_{x=1}^{x=5}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{12}{\int }_{0}^{3}5{y}^{2}-{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{12}{\int }_{0}^{3}4{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{12}{[\frac{4}{3}{y}^{3}]}_{0}^{3} \\  & =\frac{M}{12}(36-0) \\  & =3M.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{M}{6}{\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{3}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{6}{\int }_{1}^{3}[x{y}^{2}]_{x=0}^{x=3}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{6}{\int }_{1}^{3}3{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{6}[{y}^{3}]_{1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{M}{6}(27-1) \\  & =\frac{13M}{3}.\end{aligned}

"A plate of mass $M$ occupies the region $D$ bounded by the lines $y=2x,$ $x=1,$ and the $x$-axis. Its mass density at any point on the plate is given by $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{3M}{2}x.$ Find the radius of gyration of the plate about the origin." :question/worked-solution "For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{x}$ about the $x$-axis is given by
${R}_{x}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{x}$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{y}$ about the $y$-axis is given by
${R}_{y}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{y}$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by
${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

The moment of inertia about the origin is defined as

$$
{I}_{0}={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function. The region $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le 2x\}.
$$

Hence, the moment of inertia about the origin is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{0} & ={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\cdot \frac{3M}{2}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2x}{x}^{3}+x{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{[{x}^{3}y+\frac{1}{3}x{y}^{3}]}_{y=0}^{y=2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}2{x}^{4}+\frac{8}{3}{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{14}{3}{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{[\frac{14}{15}{x}^{5}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}\cdot \frac{14}{15} \\  & =\frac{7M}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of gyration about the origin is

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{0} & =\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{7M}{5}\cdot \frac{1}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{7}{5}}.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-96a67bd8-ef2e-5ca9-867f-c8028ad58f33"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-96a67bd8-ef2e-5ca9-867f-c8028ad58f33" :answer-field/id #uuid "96a67bd8-ef2e-5ca9-867f-c8028ad58f33" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/correct "answer-dac54592-73f2-5539-95af-9b181dfbbc6d" :answer-field/choices ["answer-17408f30-0e49-5024-8582-e77ea33d1531" "answer-c3244fd4-d2f9-5e9c-ab2f-2bf3f05ed94e" "answer-5c870d2c-e72b-5ed4-9ac6-a6bac8e306d7" "answer-1aa03666-f99f-5788-82b2-6a8cfc4ed4a0" "answer-dac54592-73f2-5539-95af-9b181dfbbc6d"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-17408f30-0e49-5024-8582-e77ea33d1531" :answer/id #uuid "17408f30-0e49-5024-8582-e77ea33d1531" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "1" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-c3244fd4-d2f9-5e9c-ab2f-2bf3f05ed94e" :answer/id #uuid "c3244fd4-d2f9-5e9c-ab2f-2bf3f05ed94e" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{8}{9}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-5c870d2c-e72b-5ed4-9ac6-a6bac8e306d7" :answer/id #uuid "5c870d2c-e72b-5ed4-9ac6-a6bac8e306d7" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{15}}{4}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1aa03666-f99f-5788-82b2-6a8cfc4ed4a0" :answer/id #uuid "1aa03666-f99f-5788-82b2-6a8cfc4ed4a0" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "answer-dac54592-73f2-5539-95af-9b181dfbbc6d" :answer/id #uuid "dac54592-73f2-5539-95af-9b181dfbbc6d" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\sqrt{\frac{7}{5}}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id "question-e0566907-74aa-5b66-a065-487764f08eb0" :question/id #uuid "e0566907-74aa-5b66-a065-487764f08eb0" :question/math-academy-id "q-38823" :question/problem "A plate of mass $M$ occupies the region $D$ bounded by the lines $y=x,$ $x=1,$ and the $x$-axis. The moment of inertia about the origin is defined as

$$
{I}_{0}={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function. The region $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,\sqrt{x}\le y\le 1\}.
$$

Hence, the moment of inertia about the origin is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{0} & ={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{x}}^{1}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\cdot 12Mxy\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =12M{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{x}}^{1}{x}^{3}y+x{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =12M{\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{3}{y}^{2}+\frac{1}{4}x{y}^{4}]}_{y=\sqrt{x}}^{y=1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =12M{\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{1}{2}{x}^{3}+\frac{1}{4}x)-(\frac{1}{2}{x}^{4}+\frac{1}{4}{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =12M{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{4}x+\frac{1}{4}{x}^{3}-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =12M{[\frac{1}{8}{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{16}{x}^{4}-\frac{1}{10}{x}^{5}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =12M(\frac{1}{8}+\frac{1}{16}-\frac{1}{10}) \\  & =12M\cdot \frac{7}{80} \\  & =\frac{21M}{20}.\end{aligned}

Therefore, the radius of gyration about the origin is

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{0} & =\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{21M}{20}\cdot \frac{1}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{21}{20}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\frac{21}{5}}.\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186281686 :question/worked-solution "For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186198956 :question/worked-solution "For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

Its mass density at any point is given by $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡2}.$ Find the radius of gyration of the plate about the $y$-axis." :question/worked-solution "For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{x}$ about the $x$-axis is given by
${R}_{x}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}},$

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by
${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

In polar coordinates, the region occupied by the plate is given by

$$
D=\{(r,\theta )\,:\,1\le r\le \sqrt{2},\,\,-\frac{\pi }{4}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{4}\}.
$$

The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis, in polar coordinates, is defined as

$$
{I}_{y}={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta ,
$$

where $\lambda (r,\theta )$ is the mass density function.

Also, the mass density in terms of polar coordinates is $\lambda (r,\theta )=\frac{M}{{r}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{ln}⁡2}.$
Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{M}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4}{\int }_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}r\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{M}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}({\int }_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}r\,\text{d}r)({\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4}\,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{M}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}{r}^{2}{|}_{1}^{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \theta {|}_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4} \\  & =\frac{M}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\cdot (1-\frac{1}{2})\cdot \frac{\pi }{2} \\  & =\frac{\pi M}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of gyration about the $x$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{y} & =\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{\pi M}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\cdot \frac{1}{M}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\frac{\pi }{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}}.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-d338a349-3b9f-5d71-b3f4-8e6e22455c77"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id $$

$$

Also, the mass density in terms of polar coordinates is $\lambda (r,\theta )=\frac{M}{\pi }{r}^{2}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{0} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{M}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}{r}^{5}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{M}{\pi }({\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}{r}^{5}\,\text{d}r)({\int }_{0}^{\pi }\,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{M}{\pi }\cdot \frac{1}{6}{r}^{6}{|}_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \theta {|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =\frac{M}{\pi }\cdot \frac{8}{6}\cdot \pi  \\  & =\frac{4M}{3}.\end{aligned}

${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

In polar coordinates, the region occupied by the plate is given by

$$
D=\{(r,\theta )\,:\,1\le r\le 2,\,\,\frac{\pi }{4}\le \theta \le \frac{3\pi }{4}\}.
$$

The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis, in polar coordinates, is defined as

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta ,
$$

where $\lambda (r,\theta )$ is the mass density function.

Also, the mass density in terms of polar coordinates is $\lambda (r,\theta )=\frac{M}{2r{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }.$
Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{M}{2}{\int }_{\pi /4}^{3\pi /4}{\int }_{1}^{2}{r}^{2}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{M}{2}({\int }_{1}^{2}{r}^{2}\,\text{d}r)({\int }_{\pi /4}^{3\pi /4}\,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{M}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{3}{r}^{3}{|}_{1}^{2}\cdot \theta {|}_{\pi /4}^{3\pi /4} \\  & =\frac{M}{2}\cdot \frac{7}{3}\cdot \frac{\pi }{2} \\  & =\frac{7\pi M}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of gyration about the $x$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{x} & =\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{7\pi M}{12}\cdot \frac{1}{M}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\frac{7\pi }{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186284397 :question/worked-solution "For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{x}$ about the $x$-axis is given by
${R}_{x}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{x}$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{y}$ about the $y$-axis is given by
${R}_{y}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{y}$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by
${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

In polar coordinates, the region occupied by the plate is given by

$$
D=\{(r,\theta )\,:\,0\le r\le \sqrt{3},\,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi \}.
$$

The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis, in polar coordinates, is defined as

$$
{I}_{y}={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta ,
$$

where $\lambda (r,\theta )$ is the mass density function.

Also, the mass density in terms of polar coordinates is $\lambda (r,\theta )=\frac{2}{9\pi }M{r}^{2}.$
Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{2}{9\pi }M{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}{r}^{5}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{2}{9\pi }M({\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}{r}^{5}\,\text{d}r)({\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{2}{9\pi }M\cdot \frac{1}{6}{r}^{6}{|}_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}({\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\frac{1+\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta }{2}\,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{2}{9\pi }M\cdot \frac{9}{2}\cdot {[\frac{\theta }{2}+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta }{4}]}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =\frac{M}{\pi }\cdot \pi  \\  & =M.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of gyration about the $x$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{y} & =\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{M\cdot \frac{1}{M}} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$" :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id 17592186199458 :tutorial/content "In this lesson, we discuss a concept analogous to *center of mass* that applies to rotating bodies.

Recall that the *center of mass* of a plane lamina is defined as the point $(\bar{x},\bar{y})$ in the coordinate plane where the entire mass of the lamina could be concentrated to produce the same *total moment* about the coordinate axes as the original laminar. 

Analogously, the **radius of gyration** of a plane lamina is the distance $R$ from an axis of rotation $L$ that the entire mass $M$ of the lamina would need to be concentrated to produce the same *moment of inertia* as the original lamina. 

![](images/c9/c9999bf30a93a857db731488739f0a640edc7b91de907cd772b777489a011fb8.png)

To derive an explicit formula for the radius of gyration, recall that the moment of inertia of a particle $P$ of mass $m$ at a distance of $r$ from an axis of rotation equals

$$
mr^2.
$$

So, for a particle of mass $M$ at a distance of $R$ from the axis of rotation $L,$ the moment of inertia about $L$ is given by

$$
MR^2.
$$

The radius of gyration is defined as the distance $R$ that a particle of mass $M$ must be placed to give the same moment of inertia as the original lamina. Therefore, it is the solution to the equation

$$
I = MR^2,
$$

where $I$ is the moment of inertia of the lamina about $L.$

Rearranging this equation, we find that the radius of gyration is given by

$$
R = \sqrt{\dfrac{I}{M}}.
$$" :db/ensure [:tutorial/validate]} {:db/id 17592186198500 :activity/expected-seconds 1380.0 :db/ensure [:activity/validate]}] "assertions" [["question-07899bf0-acd5-5cb5-8654-0b2936590b7d" :question/id #uuid "07899bf0-acd5-5cb5-8654-0b2936590b7d"] ["question-07899bf0-acd5-5cb5-8654-0b2936590b7d" :question/math-academy-id "q-163577"] ["question-07899bf0-acd5-5cb5-8654-0b2936590b7d" :question/problem "A rectangular plate of mass $M$ and uniform mass density occupies the region
$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,2\le x\le 3,\,\,1\le y\le 4\}.$ Find the radius of gyration of the plate about the $x$-axis."] ["question-07899bf0-acd5-5cb5-8654-0b2936590b7d" :question/worked-solution "For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{x}$ about the $x$-axis is given by
${R}_{x}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{x}$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{y}$ about the $y$-axis is given by
${R}_{y}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{y}$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by
${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is defined as

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function.

The area of the rectangular plate $D$ is $A=1\cdot 3=3.$ Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by

$$
\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{A}=\frac{M}{3}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{M}{3}{\int }_{1}^{4}{\int }_{2}^{3}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{3}{\int }_{1}^{4}[x{y}^{2}]_{x=2}^{x=3}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{3}{\int }_{1}^{4}3{y}^{2}-2{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{3}{\int }_{1}^{4}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{3}{[\frac{1}{3}{y}^{3}]}_{1}^{4} \\  & =\frac{M}{3}(\frac{64}{3}-\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =\frac{M}{3}\cdot 21 \\  & =7M.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
{R}_{x}^{2}=7\,⇒\,{R}_{x}=\sqrt{7}.
$$"] ["question-07899bf0-acd5-5cb5-8654-0b2936590b7d" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] ["answer-field-80bbb187-dc3c-5b0f-ba62-a0ca8ff3dda3" :answer-field/id #uuid :question/problem "A rectangular plate of mass $M$ and uniform mass density occupies the region
$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 5,\,\,0\le y\le 3\}.$ Find the radius of gyration of the plate about the $x$-axis."] ["question-a8f6939e-ee8d-5d31-921b-202a2621754c" :question/worked-solution "For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{x}$ about the $x$-axis is given by
${R}_{x}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{x}$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{y}$ about the $y$-axis is given by
${R}_{y}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{y}$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by
${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is defined as

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function.

The area of the rectangular plate $D$ is $A=4\cdot 3=12.$ Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by

$$
\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{A}=\frac{M}{12}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{M}{12}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{1}^{5}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{12}{\int }_{0}^{3}[x{y}^{2}]_{x=1}^{x=5}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{12}{\int }_{0}^{3}5{y}^{2}-{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{12}{\int }_{0}^{3}4{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{12}{[\frac{4}{3}{y}^{3}]}_{0}^{3} \\  & =\frac{M}{12}(36-0) \\  & =3M.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$

$$"] ["question-a8f6939e-ee8d-5d31-921b-202a2621754c" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] ["answer-field-2bb25b16-fefe-543c-8d2a-1f870068fdf2" :answer-field/id #uuid :question/problem "A rectangular plate of mass $M$ and uniform mass density occupies the region
$D=\{(x,y)\,:\,3\le x\le 5,\,\,2\le y\le 4\}.$ Find the radius of gyration of the plate about the $y$-axis."] ["question-9f4fdbea-b5e1-5c4f-b10b-d88e66b48be2" :question/worked-solution "For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{x}$ about the $x$-axis is given by
${R}_{x}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{x}$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{y}$ about the $y$-axis is given by
${R}_{y}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{y}$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by
${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is defined as

$$
{I}_{y}={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function.

The area of the rectangular plate $D$ is $A=2\cdot 2=4.$ Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by

$$
\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{A}=\frac{M}{4}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{M}{4}{\int }_{2}^{4}{\int }_{3}^{5}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{4}{\int }_{2}^{4}{[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{3}^{5}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{4}{\int }_{2}^{4}(\frac{125}{3}-9)\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{4}{\int }_{2}^{4}\frac{98}{3}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{4}{[\frac{98}{3}y]}_{2}^{4} \\  & =\frac{49M}{6}\cdot (4-2) \\  & =\frac{49M}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
{R}_{y}^{2}=\frac{49}{3}\,⇒\,{R}_{y}=\sqrt{\frac{49}{3}}=\frac{7}{\sqrt{3}}.
$$"] ["question-9f4fdbea-b5e1-5c4f-b10b-d88e66b48be2" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] ["answer-field-6481d0c5-9b18-592d-a5aa-357b3fbca57b" :answer-field/id #uuid $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 3,\,\,0\le y\le 5\}.$ Find the radius of gyration of the plate about the $x$-axis."] ["question-464dc60e-dfa3-5c24-8df3-bdca1e567180" :question/worked-solution "For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{x}$ about the $x$-axis is given by
${R}_{x}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{x}$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{y}$ about the $y$-axis is given by

where ${I}_{y}$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by

where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is defined as

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function.

The area of the rectangular plate $D$ is $A=3\cdot 5=15.$ Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by

$$
\lambda (x,y)=\frac{M}{A}=\frac{M}{15}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{M}{15}{\int }_{0}^{5}{\int }_{0}^{3}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{15}{\int }_{0}^{5}[x{y}^{2}]_{x=0}^{x=3}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{15}{\int }_{0}^{5}3{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{15}[{y}^{3}]_{0}^{5} \\  & =\frac{M}{15}(125-0) \\  & =\frac{25M}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{R}_{x}^{2}=\frac{25}{3}\,⇒\,{R}_{x}=\sqrt{\frac{25}{3}}=\frac{5}{\sqrt{3}}.
$$"] ["question-464dc60e-dfa3-5c24-8df3-bdca1e567180" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] ["answer-field-ca4abcbb-4080-56b3-9f3e-dfec3322b962" :answer-field/id #uuid :question/problem "A plate of mass $M$ occupies the region $D$ bounded by the lines $y=2x,$ $x=1,$ and the $x$-axis. Its mass density at any point on the plate is given by $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{3M}{2}x.$ Find the radius of gyration of the plate about the origin."] ["question-3441cc98-9576-5e74-bdad-b0f5fae54049" :question/worked-solution "For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{x}$ about the $x$-axis is given by
${R}_{x}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{x}$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{y}$ about the $y$-axis is given by
${R}_{y}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{y}$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by
${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

The moment of inertia about the origin is defined as

$$
{I}_{0}={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function. The region $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le 2x\}.
$$

Hence, the moment of inertia about the origin is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{0} & ={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\cdot \frac{3M}{2}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2x}{x}^{3}+x{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{[{x}^{3}y+\frac{1}{3}x{y}^{3}]}_{y=0}^{y=2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}2{x}^{4}+\frac{8}{3}{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{14}{3}{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}{[\frac{14}{15}{x}^{5}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{3M}{2}\cdot \frac{14}{15} \\  & =\frac{7M}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of gyration about the origin is

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{0} & =\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{7M}{5}\cdot \frac{1}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{7}{5}}.\end{aligned}
$$"] ["question-3441cc98-9576-5e74-bdad-b0f5fae54049" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] ["answer-field-96a67bd8-ef2e-5ca9-867f-c8028ad58f33" :answer-field/id #uuid The moment of inertia about the origin is defined as

$$
{I}_{0}={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function. The region $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le x\}.
$$

Hence, the moment of inertia about the origin is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{0} & ={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\cdot 8Mxy\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =8M{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}{x}^{3}y+x{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =8M{\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{3}{y}^{2}+\frac{1}{4}x{y}^{4}]}_{y=0}^{y=x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =8M{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{2}{x}^{5}+\frac{1}{4}{x}^{5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =8M{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3}{4}{x}^{5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =M{\int }_{0}^{1}6{x}^{5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =M[{x}^{6}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =M.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{0} & =\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{M}{M}} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$"] ["question-e0566907-74aa-5b66-a065-487764f08eb0" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] ["answer-field-f86770b1-e70e-5836-9012-fa9db97a322a" :answer-field/id #uuid $$

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by
${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

In polar coordinates, the region occupied by the plate is given by

$$
D=\{(r,\theta )\,:\,1\le r\le \sqrt{2},\,\,-\frac{\pi }{4}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{4}\}.
$$

The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis, in polar coordinates, is defined as

$$
{I}_{y}={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta ,

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{y} & =\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{\pi M}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\cdot \frac{1}{M}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\frac{\pi }{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}}.\end{aligned}

lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{x}$ about the $x$-axis is given by
${R}_{x}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{x}$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{y}$ about the $y$-axis is given by
${R}_{y}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{y}$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by
${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

In polar coordinates, the region occupied by the plate is given by

$$
D=\{(r,\theta )\,:\,1\le r\le 2,\,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi \}.
$$

The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis, in polar coordinates, is defined as

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta ,
$$

where $\lambda (r,\theta )$ is the mass density function.

Also, the mass density in terms of polar coordinates is $\lambda (r,\theta )=\frac{3}{14\pi }Mr.$
Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{3}{14\pi }M{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{1}^{2}{r}^{4}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{3M}{14\pi }({\int }_{1}^{2}{r}^{4}\,\text{d}r)({\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{3M}{14\pi }\cdot \frac{1}{5}{r}^{5}{|}_{1}^{2}\cdot ({\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\frac{(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta )}{2}\,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{3M}{14\pi }\cdot \frac{31}{5}\cdot {[\frac{1}{2}\theta -\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta ]}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =\frac{3M}{14\pi }\cdot \frac{31}{5}\cdot \pi  \\  & =\frac{93M}{70}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of gyration about the $x$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{x} & =\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{93M}{70}\cdot \frac{1}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{93}{70}}.\end{aligned}
$$"] [17592186369943 :question/worked-solution "For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{x}$ about the $x$-axis is given by
${R}_{x}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{x}$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{y}$ about the $y$-axis is given by
${R}_{y}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{y}$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by
${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

In polar coordinates, the region occupied by the plate is given by

$$
D=\{(r,\theta )\,:\,1\le r\le 2,\,\,\frac{\pi }{4}\le \theta \le \frac{3\pi }{4}\}.
$$

The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis, in polar coordinates, is defined as

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta ,
$$

where $\lambda (r,\theta )$ is the mass density function.

Also, the mass density in terms of polar coordinates is $\lambda (r,\theta )=\frac{M}{2r{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }.$
Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{M}{2}{\int }_{\pi /4}^{3\pi /4}{\int }_{1}^{2}{r}^{2}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{M}{2}({\int }_{1}^{2}{r}^{2}\,\text{d}r)({\int }_{\pi /4}^{3\pi /4}\,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{M}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{3}{r}^{3}{|}_{1}^{2}\cdot \theta {|}_{\pi /4}^{3\pi /4} \\  & =\frac{M}{2}\cdot \frac{7}{3}\cdot \frac{\pi }{2} \\  & =\frac{7\pi M}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of gyration about the $x$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{x} & =\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{7\pi M}{12}\cdot \frac{1}{M}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\frac{7\pi }{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$"] [17592186284397 :question/worked-solution "For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{x}$ about the $x$-axis is given by
${R}_{x}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{x}$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{y}$ about the $y$-axis is given by
${R}_{y}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{y}$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by
${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

In polar coordinates, the region occupied by the plate is given by

$$
D=\{(r,\theta )\,:\,0\le r\le \sqrt{3},\,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi \}.
$$

The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis, in polar coordinates, is defined as

$$
{I}_{y}={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta ,
$$

where $\lambda (r,\theta )$ is the mass density function.

Also, the mass density in terms of polar coordinates is $\lambda (r,\theta )=\frac{2}{9\pi }M{r}^{2}.$
Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{2}{9\pi }M{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}{r}^{5}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{2}{9\pi }M({\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}{r}^{5}\,\text{d}r)({\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{2}{9\pi }M\cdot \frac{1}{6}{r}^{6}{|}_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}({\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\frac{1+\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta }{2}\,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{2}{9\pi }M\cdot \frac{9}{2}\cdot {[\frac{\theta }{2}+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta }{4}]}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =\frac{M}{\pi }\cdot \pi  \\  & =M.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of gyration about the $x$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{y} & =\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{M\cdot \frac{1}{M}} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$"] [17592186199458 :tutorial/content "In this lesson, we discuss a concept analogous to *center of mass* that applies to rotating bodies.

Recall that the *center of mass* of a plane lamina is defined as the point $(\bar{x},\bar{y})$ in the coordinate plane where the entire mass of the lamina could be concentrated to produce the same *total moment* about the coordinate axes as the original laminar. 

Analogously, the **radius of gyration** of a plane lamina is the distance $R$ from an axis of rotation $L$ that the entire mass $M$ of the lamina would need to be concentrated to produce the same *moment of inertia* as the original lamina. 

![](images/c9/c9999bf30a93a857db731488739f0a640edc7b91de907cd772b777489a011fb8.png)

To derive an explicit formula for the radius of gyration, recall that the moment of inertia of a particle $P$ of mass $m$ at a distance of $r$ from an axis of rotation equals

$$
mr^2.
$$

So, for a particle of mass $M$ at a distance of $R$ from the axis of rotation $L,$ the moment of inertia about $L$ is given by

$$
MR^2.
$$

The radius of gyration is defined as the distance $R$ that a particle of mass $M$ must be placed to give the same moment of inertia as the original lamina. Therefore, it is the solution to the equation

$$
I = MR^2,
$$

where $I$ is the moment of inertia of the lamina about $L.$

Rearranging this equation, we find that the radius of gyration is given by

$$
R = \sqrt{\dfrac{I}{M}}.
$$"] [17592186198500 :activity/expected-seconds 1380.0]] "retractions" [[17592186281682 :question/worked-solution "For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

The moment of inertia about the origin is defined as

$$
{I}_{0}={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function. The region $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,\sqrt{x}\le y\le 1}.

Hence, the moment of inertia about the origin is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{0} & ={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{x}}^{1}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\cdot 12Mxy\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =12M{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{x}}^{1}{x}^{3}y+x{y}^{3}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =12M{\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{3}{y}^{2}+\frac{1}{4}x{y}^{4}]}_{y=\sqrt{x}}^{y=1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =12M{\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{1}{2}{x}^{3}+\frac{1}{4}x)-(\frac{1}{2}{x}^{4}+\frac{1}{4}{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =12M{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{4}x+\frac{1}{4}{x}^{3}-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =12M{[\frac{1}{8}{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{16}{x}^{4}-\frac{1}{10}{x}^{5}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =12M(\frac{1}{8}+\frac{1}{16}-\frac{1}{10}) \\  & =12M\cdot \frac{7}{80} \\  & =\frac{21M}{20}.\end{aligned}

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by
${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

In polar coordinates, the region occupied by the plate is given by

$$
D={(r,\theta )\,:\,0\le r\le \sqrt{3},\,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi }.
$$

The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis, in polar coordinates, is defined as

$$
{I}_{y}={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta ,
$$

where $\lambda (r,\theta )$ is the mass density function.

Also, the mass density in terms of polar coordinates is $\lambda (r,\theta )=\frac{2}{9\pi }M{r}^{2}.$
Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{2}{9\pi }M{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}{r}^{5}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{2}{9\pi }M({\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}{r}^{5}\,\text{d}r)({\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{2}{9\pi }M\cdot \frac{1}{6}{r}^{6}{|}_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}({\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\frac{1+\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta }{2}\,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{2}{9\pi }M\cdot \frac{9}{2}\cdot {[\frac{\theta }{2}+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta }{4}]}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =\frac{M}{\pi }\cdot \pi  \\  & =M.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of gyration about the $x$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{y} & =\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{M\cdot \frac{1}{M}} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$"] [17592186199458 :tutorial/content "In this lesson, we discuss a concept analogous to *center of mass* that applies to rotating bodies.

Recall that the *center of mass* of a plane lamina is defined as the point $(\bar{x},\bar{y})$ in the coordinate plane where the entire mass of the lamina could be concentrated to produce the same *total moment* about the coordinate axes as the original laminar. 

Analogously, the **radius of gyration** of a plane lamina is the distance $R$ from an axis of rotation $L$ that the entire mass $M$ of the lamina would need to be concentrated to produce the same *moment of inertia* as the original lamina. 

![](images/c9/c9999bf30a93a857db731488739f0a640edc7b91de907cd772b777489a011fb8.png)

To derive an explicit formula for the radius of gyration, recall that the moment of inertia of a particle $P$ of mass $m$ at a distance of $r$ from an axis of rotation equals

$$
mr^2.
$$

Now, suppose that a plane lamina of mass [math]M[/math] occupies the region [math]D \subset \mathbb{R}^2[/math] and rotates about a line [math]L.[/math]

So, for a particle of mass $M$ at a distance of $R$ from the axis of rotation $L,$ the moment of inertia about $L$ is given by

$$
MR^2.
$$

The radius of gyration is defined as the distance $R$ that a particle of mass $M$ must be placed to give the same moment of inertia as the original lamina. Therefore, it is the solution to the equation

$$
I = MR^2,
$$

where $I$ is the moment of inertia of the lamina about $L.$

Rearranging this equation, we find that the radius of gyration is given by

$$
R = \sqrt{\dfrac{I}{M}}.
$$"]]}

$D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 3, \:\: 1 \leq y \leq 2 \big\}.$ Find the radius of gyration of the plate about the $y$-axis." :question/worked-solution "For a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ with mass $M$ and mass density function $\lambda(x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The radius of gyration $R_x$ about the $x$-axis is given by
$R_x = \sqrt{\dfrac{I_x}{M}},$
where $I_x$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

- The radius of gyration $R_y$ about the $y$-axis is given by
$R_y = \sqrt{\dfrac{I_y}{M}},$
where $I_y$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

- The radius of gyration $R_0$ about the origin is given by
$R_0 = \sqrt{\dfrac{I_0}{M}},$
where $I_0$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is defined as

$$
I_y = \iint\limits_D x^2\lambda(x,y) \:\textrm{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda(x,y)$ is the mass density function.

The area of the rectangular plate $D$ is $\mathcal{A} =  3\cdot 1 = 3.$ Since the plate has uniform density, the mass density function is given by

$$
\lambda(x,y) = \dfrac{M}{\mathcal{A}} = \dfrac{M}{3}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{M}{3}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{3}{\int }_{1}^{2}{[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{0}^{3}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{M}{3}{\int }_{1}^{2}9\,\text{d}y \\  & =3M{\int }_{1}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =3M[y]_{1}^{2} \\  & =3M(2-1) \\  & =3M.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
R_y^2 =\dfrac{3M}{M} =  3\quad \Rightarrow\quad R_y = \sqrt{3}.
$$"} {:db/id 17592186049331} {:db/id 17592186198651 :question/id #uuid "5e1eb104-83e6-5dc7-913b-3996107f92c0" :question/math-academy-id "q-163011"} {:db/id 17592186198665 :question/id #uuid $R_y = \sqrt{\dfrac{I_y}{M}},$
where $I_y$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

- The radius of gyration $R_0$ about the origin is given by
$R_0 = \sqrt{\dfrac{I_0}{M}},$
where $I_0$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

In polar coordinates, the region occupied by the plate is given by

$$
D = \left\{ (r,\theta) \: : \: 0 \leq r \leq 1, \:\: 0 \leq \theta \leq \pi \right\}.
$$

The moment of inertia about the origin, in polar coordinates, is defined as

$$
I_0 = \iint\limits_D \lambda(r,\theta) r^3 \:\textrm{d}r\:\textrm{d}\theta,
$$

where $\lambda(r,\theta)$ is the mass density function.

Also, the mass density in terms of polar coordinates is $\lambda(r,\theta)=\dfrac{3}{2}Mr\sin\theta.$
Therefore, the moment of inertia about the origin is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{0} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{3}{2}M{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{1}{r}^{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{3}{2}M({\int }_{0}^{1}{r}^{4}\,\text{d}r)({\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}M\cdot \frac{1}{5}{r}^{5}{|}_{0}^{1}\cdot (-\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ){|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =\frac{3}{2}M\cdot \frac{1}{5}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{3M}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of gyration about the origin is

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{0} & =\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{3M}{5}\cdot \frac{1}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{3}{5}}.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186198663 :question/id #uuid "b31c8b99-cc6d-5598-a2c8-85f537ed1a0d" :question/math-academy-id "q-163586"} {:db/id 17592186198957 :question/id #uuid - The radius of gyration ${R}_{x}$ about the $x$-axis is given by

where ${I}_{x}$ is the moment of inertia about the $x$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{y}$ about the $y$-axis is given by
${R}_{y}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{y}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{y}$ is the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis.

- The radius of gyration ${R}_{0}$ about the origin is given by
${R}_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{0}}{M}},$
where ${I}_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the origin.

In polar coordinates, the region occupied by the plate is given by

$$
D={(r,\theta )\,:\,1\le r\le 2,\,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi }.
$$

The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis, in polar coordinates, is defined as

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta ,
$$

where $\lambda (r,\theta )$ is the mass density function.

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{x} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (r,\theta ){r}^{3}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{3}{14\pi }M{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{1}^{2}{r}^{4}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{3M}{14\pi }({\int }_{1}^{2}{r}^{4}\,\text{d}r)({\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{3M}{14\pi }\cdot \frac{1}{5}{r}^{5}{|}_{1}^{2}\cdot ({\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\frac{(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta )}{2}\,\text{d}\theta ) \\  & =\frac{3M}{14\pi }\cdot \frac{31}{5}\cdot {[\frac{1}{2}\theta -\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta ]}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =\frac{3M}{14\pi }\cdot \frac{31}{5}\cdot \pi  \\  & =\frac{93M}{70}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of gyration about the $x$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{x} & =\sqrt{\frac{{I}_{x}}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{93M}{70}\cdot \frac{1}{M}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{93}{70}}.\end{aligned}
$$"} {:db/id 17592186284393 :question/id #uuid "394b0509-9101-5b75-8b23-1291af4adfe7" :question/math-academy-id "q-163650"} {:db/id 17592186284394 :question/id #uuid
